bb_captain.text: Sir William Alexander Smith was born here in 1854. He moved to Glasgow, taught Sunday school, and found the boys bored stiff. So in 1883 he gave them drill, games, camp and a wee pillbox hat. The Boys' Brigade.
It was the first uniformed youth organisation of its kind, before the Scouts. Baden-Powell himself was a vice-president of the Brigade, and he got some of his ideas from it.
'Sure and Stedfast', that's the motto, with one 'a' in stedfast. Every Brigade boy gets that spelling test.
